pattern: Search is a derived read model (CQRS): stream changes from the source of truth into a partitioned inverted index, tier it by time so fresh data stays small and fast, and answer queries by scatter-gather with cheap per-shard scoring and a global re-rank.

checks.label: Core use case captured

tips.nudge: What does the user type, and what comes back?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for searching posts by words.
tips.show: F1: A user searches public posts by keywords (and phrases/hashtags) and gets matching posts.

checks.label: How soon a new post must be findable

tips.nudge: Something big happens. People search for it within seconds. Must the first posts about it show up?
tips.hint: State the time from posting to searchable.
tips.show: N2: A new post is searchable within ~10 s.

checks.label: Query speed expectation stated

tips.nudge: The interviewer gave you a number for a search.
tips.hint: State a latency target for a search request.
tips.show: N1: Search p99 < 500 ms, even during event spikes.

checks.label: What happens when a post goes away captured

tips.nudge: A user deletes a post or makes it private. What should search show a minute later?
tips.hint: Add a requirement about deleted or hidden posts.
tips.show: F4: Deleted or hidden posts disappear from results within ~1 minute.

checks.label: Ingest throughput estimated

tips.nudge: Start from posts per day.
tips.hint: posts/day ÷ seconds in a day; then a peak factor.
tips.show: 500M / day ≈ 5.8k posts/s (peak ~15k/s).

checks.label: Query throughput estimated

tips.nudge: Searches per day, then the event spike.
tips.hint: searches/day ÷ seconds in a day × spike factor.
tips.show: 200M / day ≈ 2.3k/s; ×5 during big events ≈ 12k/s.

checks.label: Index size estimated

tips.nudge: How many posts are searchable, and how much index does each one cost?
tips.hint: posts over the retention × bytes of postings per post (~30 terms).
tips.show: 500M × 365 × 5 ≈ 900B posts × ~300 B ≈ 270 TB of index.

checks.label: Search endpoint defined

tips.nudge: What does the app send, and how does it page?
tips.hint: A GET with the query, a mode (top vs latest) and a cursor.
tips.show: GET /search?q=&mode=top|latest&cursor= → {posts[], next_cursor}

checks.label: The searchable item modelled

tips.nudge: What fields of a post does search need?
tips.hint: Distinguish the source of truth from what goes into the index.
tips.show: posts(post_id time-sortable, author_id, text, lang, created_at, visibility) in the posts store; indexed doc = post_id, terms, created_at, author, lang.

checks.label: How text is looked up modelled

tips.nudge: Scanning 900 billion posts for a word is not an option. What structure maps words to posts?
tips.hint: Model the index itself: what is the key, what is the value, how is it ordered?
tips.show: Inverted index: term → posting list of post_ids (sorted newest first) + positions; per-shard, per-time-tier segments.

checks.label: Getting posts into the index designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Should the post service write to the index while the author waits?
tips.hint: Add a part for the ingestion pipeline: compare a synchronous dual write, batch reindexing and an event stream.
tips.show: Part 'Ingestion pipeline': post created/deleted events (outbox/CDC) on Kafka; indexer workers tokenize and write to the real-time index within seconds.

checks.label: Splitting the index designed as its own part

tips.nudge: 270 TB of index won't fit one machine. Do you split by word or by post?
tips.hint: Add a part for index partitioning: term-partitioned vs document-partitioned, plus time tiers and replicas.
tips.show: Part 'Index partitioning': document-partitioned shards inside time tiers (real-time, recent, archive), each shard replicated for query throughput.

checks.label: Answering a query designed as its own part

tips.nudge: One query, hundreds of shards, 500 ms. Who asks whom, and who decides the order?
tips.hint: Add a part for query execution: how shards are queried, merged and ranked, and what happens with slow shards.
tips.show: Part 'Query fan-out and ranking': a broker scatters to relevant tiers, each shard returns its top-k by a cheap score, the broker merges and re-ranks the top ~1000 with engagement features; timeouts and hedged requests bound the tail.

checks.label: Freshness designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A post from 5 seconds ago and a like from 1 second ago both matter. Reindex on every like?
tips.hint: Add a part for recency: how new posts become searchable fast and how changing signals reach ranking.
tips.show: Part 'Recency': an in-memory real-time tier refreshed every second serves new posts and 'Latest'; likes/reposts update a separate signals store read at ranking time instead of reindexing.

checks.label: Text lookup that doesn't scan every post

tips.nudge: How do you find posts containing a word without reading all of them?
tips.hint: Add the component that holds the inverted index.
tips.show: A search cluster (Elasticsearch/Lucene-style) holding inverted-index shards.

checks.label: Traffic spread across instances

tips.nudge: Thousands of searches per second, ×5 during events.
tips.hint: Stateless brokers behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: Clients → load balancer → stateless post and search broker instances.

checks.label: Index updated off the posting request

tips.nudge: Who writes into the index, and is the author waiting for it?
tips.hint: Let an asynchronous consumer, not the request, write to the index.
tips.show: Post service → post events stream → indexer workers → real-time index.

checks.label: Removing posts from immutable segments decided

tips.nudge: Index segments are immutable. How does a deleted post vanish within a minute?
tips.hint: Compare rewriting segments with marking documents as deleted and filtering.
tips.show: Delete event → tombstone (deleted-docs bitset) in every tier; queries filter tombstones; segments are purged on the next merge.

checks.label: Bottlenecks and single points of failure named

tips.nudge: Which part hurts first when a big event breaks?
tips.hint: Walk the ingest path and the query path separately.
tips.show: Real-time tier write + query load during events (more replicas), hot queries (short-TTL result cache), slowest shard sets the tail (hedging, partial results), indexer lag (scale consumers).

checks.label: Growth plan described

tips.nudge: Posts ×10. What grows: shards, replicas, or both?
tips.hint: Separate data growth from query growth.
tips.show: More data → more shards per tier (doc-partitioned, add a new time tier); more queries → more replicas; old tiers on cheaper, disk-heavy nodes.
